images.title: One group of the grid
images.purpose: Show that sharing the 21 squares into 3 equal groups gives 7 squares for 1/3, and into 7 equal groups gives 3 squares for 1/7.
images.composition: Two copies of the same 3 by 7 grid: the left shared into 3 columns with 1 column shaded, the right shared into 7 rows with 1 row shaded.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 62, the heading A grid of 21 squares in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). Two identical grids stand side by side. Each grid is 3 columns by 7 rows of equal squares, every square 72 by 72 px, so each grid is 216 px wide and 504 px tall and has 21 squares; thin dark #2B2B2B grid lines (2 px) and a 3 px outer outline. LEFT GRID: x 340 to 556, y 120 to 624. Two thick dark vertical lines (6 px) run down the full height between column 1 and column 2 and between column 2 and column 3, so the grid is cut into 3 equal groups of 7 squares, one group per column. Column 1 (the left column, 7 squares, x 340 to 412) is filled teal #0072B2; the other 14 squares are white. RIGHT GRID: x 900 to 1116, y 120 to 624. Six thick dark horizontal lines (6 px) run across the full width between each pair of neighbouring rows, so the grid is cut into 7 equal groups of 3 squares, one group per row. Row 1 (the top row, 3 squares, y 120 to 192) is filled amber #E69F00; the other 18 squares are white. Under the left grid, centred at x 448 and y 690, the caption 1/3 = 7 squares; under the right grid, centred at x 1008 and y 690, the caption 1/7 = 3 squares, both dark #1F2937 bold (48 px). No other text, no numbers inside the squares. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a grid with a row or column count other than 3 columns and 7 rows, or groups of unequal size
images.takeaway: To find 1/n of a grid, share its squares into n equal groups: 21 squares make 7 in each of 3 groups and 3 in each of 7 groups.
images.description: Two grids of 3 columns by 7 rows: in the first one column of 7 squares is shaded for 1/3, in the second one row of 3 squares is shaded for 1/7.
images.context: Concept image for Finding a Fraction of a Grid. It follows the idea of the figure in your maths book (a grid shared into equal groups with one group shaded) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 3 columns and 7 rows.
images.teaching_notes: Count the squares of one group together, then check that the groups add back to 21. The slip to watch: dividing the squares into unequal groups, or naming the group by its square count instead of by how many groups there are.

image_decisions.why: The 21 squares shared into equal groups make 'one group is 1/n' countable, which words alone do not.
